Then the angel tells her to humble herself under her mistress's hands, and the story, although needing longer accounts, has been summarized for us. Now we are left to show the image of our Savior, for whom this broad word has been spoken to us. The divine Paul, having summarized the story in a few words, has brought together a catalog of long accounts into one theory, making the unattractive thing into a more charming image of things. He writes to someone, saying that the law should not be despised, for it is written that Abraham had two sons, one from a slave and one from a free woman, and these are allegorized as two covenants, one from Mount Sinai, which gives birth to slavery, and the other from the free woman, which is our mother, the heavenly Jerusalem.

Not as having something better to say, lest one fall into madness, thinking to conceive something greater or better than what the herald of truth has pointed out, but since nothing hinders exercise, let us bring forth more natural thoughts, and as if with various colors, let us adorn the image, and through the same characters, let us come to the same schema of allegory. Take Abraham, who represents the ancient world and the nature of humanity, shown through the female and old age. The nature of humanity is the most ancient and fertile, having lived for a long time, enclosed in a single pasture, like the firmament. This free nature of humanity, created by God, has been allotted to rule all things, running alongside time, but having no genuine and God-given child, it delights in alien and illegitimate children, namely those from Egypt, that is, from darkness. Egypt is interpreted as darkness. What is this darkness? Is it not the false wisdom of the world, under which the ancient wise men were born, like offspring of a wandering rabbit, and they were sons of the age? The Savior called them thus. They were illegitimate, nonetheless, and were raised as servants, for they served gods not by nature.

Since time has grown old and is coming to an end, the Son promised has been given, and human nature, which is idle and useless, like nothing, barren and childless, has given birth to a noble child, one of the chosen from the many; then the heir, our Lord Jesus Christ, appears; the servant girl is cast out with her children; where is the wise man, the scribe, the debater of this age, for God has made foolish the wisdom of the world; the one from the free woman still inherits; the Father says to the Son, ask and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession; a divine goodness does not allow the cast-out servant girl to perish with her children; she is sent back and told to humble herself under the hands of the free woman; for the false wisdom of the world, which once mocked the marriages of the free, now serves the noble children of God through the most noble agreement of words, serving divine spectacles; the birth of Isaac from the promise signifies nothing other than the birth of Christ at the end of the ages; let no one be troubled if not all parts of the story are applied to the truth; for allegorical interpretations are introduced against the possible meanings

Since the righteous is often compared to a sheep due to the gentleness in the animal, it is completely unbelievable to say that he would be goring or butting with horns. We must yield to the demonstration of the things at hand. For it is necessary, I think, for Christ to appear in the generation according to Isaac, as if formed through a type. Lest I seem to be using superfluous and idle words, and trying to wise up the truth from every direction, and to compose images in another way, weaving together notions and conjectures, let us again place ourselves beside the divine Scripture, so that I may be speaking the truth. God did not make the promise to Abraham for the sake of anyone else, but for the sake of our Savior's sojourn, on which the conclusion of the blessing depends. I will set before you the divine word, which declares: 'I will bless her, and I will give you a child from her, and I will bless him, and he will be for nations, and kings of nations will come out from him.' And again: 'I will establish my covenant with him as an eternal covenant, and with his seed after him.' It is clear that Isaac became the father of one son, and the blessed Jacob sprang only from him; and Jacob had twelve children, but only one tribe, that of the Jews, was given from them.

How will the statement 'It will be for the nations' be fulfilled? If the nation from Israel is divided into twelve tribes, it is still one nation, composed of many members, but filled into one body through all. But again, it will not be an eternal covenant from God to those from the seed of Isaac, as the covenant defined through Moses. The prophet Joel says, 'Behold, days are coming,' says the Lord, 'and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.' Paul understands this well and says, 'When he says new, he has made the first one old; the old and aging one is near disappearance.' Therefore, there has been an annulment of the previous command, and an introduction of a better hope, through which we approach God. Therefore, it has been demonstrated everywhere that Abraham, who is from one nation, has become the father of many nations; but another argument forces us to consider the truth written about him, and it is necessary to bring Christ into the promise. He was the one, as I already said, depicted in that passage. He has become the father of many nations, drawing all to himself through faith, and rejoicing in the multitude of nations, saying, 'Behold, I and the children God has given me.' These things are about him. Let Paul, the wisest, also be a witness to the truth, and let him struggle together with me, saying…

The one supplying the Spirit to you and working powers in you, from works of law or from hearing of faith, as Abraham believed God and was reckoned to him for righteousness. You know therefore that those from faith, these are sons of Abraham. The power of the promise will be for those not just born according to flesh, but for those who through faith in Christ are inscribed as father Abraham's. For it seems to me that the blessed Baptist says to those from Israel, when they were boasting about their fleshly connection, presenting Abraham as the ancestor of the race. He says, 'Make fruits worthy of repentance, and do not think to say among yourselves, we have Abraham as father.' For God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.

As the divine word declares, 'I will bless her, and I will give you a child from her, and I will bless him, and he will be for nations, and kings of nations will come out from him.' (Genesis 17:16) The covenant is eternal, and its conclusion is tied to the sojourn of our Savior. It is clear that Isaac became the father of one son, Jacob, and the blessed Jacob sprang only from him; and Jacob had twelve children, but only one tribe, that of the Jews, was given from them.

This is because the covenant defined through Moses is not an eternal covenant from God to those from the seed of Isaac. Therefore, there has been an annulment of the previous command, and an introduction of a better hope, through which we approach God. It has been demonstrated that Abraham, who is from one nation, has become the father of many nations, and it is necessary to bring Christ into the promise. He was the one depicted in that passage, and he has become the father of many nations, drawing all to himself through faith, and rejoicing in the multitude of nations. Let Paul, the wisest, also be a witness to the truth, and let him struggle together with me, saying that the promise of God is fulfilled in Christ.

The one who supplies the Spirit to you and works powers in you does so not because of your works of law, but because of your hearing of faith, just as Abraham believed God and was reckoned to him for righteousness (Galatians 3:6). This is why you know that those who are from faith are the true sons of Abraham. The power of the promise, therefore, will be for those who are not just born according to the flesh, but for those who, through their faith in Christ, are inscribed as children of Abraham.

The blessed Baptist said to those from Israel, when they were boasting about their fleshly connection and presenting Abraham as the ancestor of their race, 'Make fruits worthy of repentance, and do not think to say among yourselves, we have Abraham as our father.' (Matthew 3:9) For God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.

ἀποδεδειγμένου σα φῶς, ὅτι περ ὁ ἐξ Ἀβραὰμ, ἑνὸς ἔθνους γέγονε πατήρ· ἑτέρου δὲ
πάλιν ἐπαναγκάζοντος λόγου δει κνύειν τὸ ἐπ' αὐτῷ γεγραμμένον ἀληθὲς
(ἀδύνατον γὰρ ψεύσασθαι Θεὸν), ἀνάγκη λοιπὸν ἐπ' αὐτὸν ἤδη φέρειν Χριστὸν τῆς
ἐπαγγελίας τὴν ἔκβασιν. Αὐτὸς γὰρ ἦν, καθάπερ ἤδη προεῖπον, ἐν ἐκείνῳ ζωγρα
φούμενος. Αὐτὸς γέγονε πατὴρ πολλῶν ἐθνῶν, πάντας μὲν διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἕλκων
ὡς ἑαυτὸν, ἐπὶ δὲ τῇ τῶν ἐθνῶν πληθύϊ καὶ μάλα γαννύμενος, καὶ λέγων· "Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ
καὶ τὰ παιδία μου, ἃ ἔδωκεν ὁ Θεός." Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν περὶ τούτων ἡμεῖς. Εἰσίτω δὲ καὶ
αὐτὸς τῆς ἀληθείας ὁ μάρτυς, ἐπαγωνιζέσθω τοῖς 77.488 εἰρημένοις ὁ σοφώτατος
Παῦλος, βοάτω σὺν ἐμοί· "Ὁ οὖν ἐπιχορηγῶν ὑμῖν τὸ Πνεῦμα, καὶ ἐνεργῶν δυνάμεις
ἐν ὑμῖν ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἢ ἐξ ἀκοῆς πίστεως, καθὼς Ἀβραὰμ ἐπίστευσε τῷ Θεῷ, καὶ
ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην." Γινώσκετε ἄρα ὅτι οἱ ἐκ πίστεως, οὗτοί εἰσιν υἱοὶ
Ἀβραάμ. Οὐκοῦν βαδιεῖται τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἡ δύναμις, οὐ πάντως εἰς τοὺς κατὰ σάρκα
γεγονότας υἱοὺς, ἀλλ' ἐπ' ἐκείνους δηλαδὴ, ὅσοιπερ ἂν διὰ τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν πίστεως
ἐπιγράψων ται πατέρα τὸν Ἀβραάμ. Τοῦτο γὰρ δή μοι καὶ διαῤῥήδην φαίνεται λέγων
ὁ μακάριος Βαπτιστὴς τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ γεγονόσιν, ὅτε δὴ καὶ ἐπὶ μόνῃ τῇ κατὰ σάρκα
κοινωνίᾳ μεγαλαυχούμενοι, ἀρχέτην τοῦ γένους προετείνοντο τὸν Ἀβραάμ·
"Ποιήσατε οὖν, φησὶ, καρποὺς ἀξίους τῆς μετανοίας, καὶ μὴ δόξητε λέγειν ἐν
ἑαυτοῖς, ὅτι Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ. ∆ύναται γὰρ ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ὁ Θεὸς
ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ." Καὶ λίθους ἐνθάδε φησὶ τοὺς ἀπεσκληκότα μὲν ἔτι
